articles.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: don’t want to get your Big Winter Coat out just yet? Try ‘onion dressing’
articles.summary: It’s time to learn the art of layering – and we’re talking a crew neck with a ballet wrap and blazer, not full-on outdoor explorer. Is layering an art? Probably not in the traditional sense. We are not talking the Bayeux tapestry here.
body: The avant-garde layering term to drop in order to sound like a connoisseur this season is onion dressing. Not the most romantic name, but a clear visual for the most refined form of layering, which is fine layers rather than hefty ones. And instead of the top layer covering all beneath it, each piece should be visible. As if we were slicing through the onion and looking at a cross-section if you will excuse me labouring the allium thing. This is layering with finesse rather than brute force. Hems and collars and cuffs give an outfit depth and texture without adding too much bulk. You want to look intriguing and multi-dimensional, not like Joey in Friends wearing all of Chandler’s clothes.
points: It’s time to learn the art of layering – and we’re talking a crew neck with a ballet wrap and blazer, not full-on outdoor explorer.

articles.title: No hands required: I found the six best slip-on shoes after months of testing
articles.summary: After a back injury, bending to put on shoes was unimaginable. I’ve since been testing pairs easy to glide my feet into – and on the eyes. What do you want to know about kitchen and food safety? Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I popped a disc in my spine a few months back, and one of the things that saved me a lot of pain during my recovery was slip-on shoes. With these, I could wear shoes that looked normal without the pain of bending over to put them on and do up the laces. I have been testing new pairs since then, looking at the various ways that manufacturers such as Kizik, Skechers and others create a shoe that you can slip on as easily as a pair of slippers, but which still look like normal shoes you could wear to work, socializing or anywhere.

I tested seven different pairs of shoes, rating them for ease of use, style, comfort and the intangibles that make you feel comfortable and more confident, no matter how much your back might be aching.

I have tested consumer products ranging from automatic coffee makers to Xbox peripherals for publications including PC World, Reviewed.com, CNET and many others. For all of those publications, I bring an objective scientific eye to testing products and helping consumers make better buying decisions. For the Filter US, I’ve tested the best gadgets if you live with back pain, the Kiziks hands-free shoes and an eco-friendly mattress.

articles.title: I’ve booked my first proper holiday – and it’s pulled me out of winter grimness like a magic spell
articles.summary: Anticipating a potential spring in which I am bathed in sun on a Greek island is giving me the kind of glee that makes anything feel possible. Reader, it’s important to tell you that I’ve never been to Greece in my life. Not once. But I might be going, for the very first time, in the spring.
body: More than the treat of a fortnight somewhere far away and yet in the company of old, dear friends, what I’m feeling most acutely is the pleasure of a promise. Having something to look forward to? A balm in the best of times. But especially so right now. I am re-emerging from beneath the cloud of the fourth (and fifth!) trimester. I read – and finished – a book the other week. I worked out with a kettlebell at some point in the past month. I went to a gig! Things are feeling viable again.

Outside of my little sphere, having something pleasurable on the horizon feels like a magic spell. There is a grimness to reading headlines in the morning that can’t be shaken off. Going on holiday clearly won’t solve these problems but my Cretan dreams give my soul small moments of uncomplicated anticipatory glee that make life worth living despite the horrors of near and far. Spring will come again, as it always does. The human race trudges on.

Perhaps I feel my most human when I am anticipating. Inside of that anticipation is the incredible knowledge that while everything is possible, sometimes I get to imagine only delightful things. It’s an excellent exercise. Like I said, a magic spell.

articles.title: Take This Step Now to Avoid Being Locked Out of Your Spotify Family Account
articles.summary: If you are on a Spotify Family plan, you may need to verify your location to keep your account active. Like many streaming services, Spotify is cracking down on family sharing for users who don't live in the same household by requiring QR code verification for some plan members—and once prompted…
body: Spotify does require users on shared plans to verify their address when they join to confirm that they live with the plan manager and to re-verify if the manager changes addresses. Users may also be prompted via to re-enter their full address if Spotify "can't confirm" their location. This obviously doesn't prevent users from sharing plans, as Spotify isn't actually tracking your location but rather cross-checking addresses.

Some users may start seeing a QR code verification requirement, which has stricter parameters and may be more difficult to get around if plan members aren't in the same location. In these cases, the plan manager must open a QR code on their phone via Profile > Your Premium > Manage, and plan members must scan it with the camera on their phone.

According to Spotify's support page, both users must be in the same location to complete the scan, and the QR code changes every few seconds, making it hard to send screenshots to anyone not present in person. However, as 9to5Google notes, some users have been able to work around these restrictions with video calls, using multiple devices to complete the scans.
points: If you are on a Spotify Family plan, you may need to verify your location to keep your account active.

articles.summary: Make every night like vacation with these hospitality expert-recommended picks.
body: If you’ve ever felt like you get the best sleep at a hotel, you’re not alone. It’s a common sentiment amongst travelers, and one I definitely know well. Whether it’s my body sinking into vacation mode, those crisp white sheets, or a little bit of both, there’s a reason why sleeping at a luxury hotel feels deeply restorative in a way that’s tough to achieve on a regular basis.

Recently, I’ve found myself feeling excited to return home after a long trip, but less enthused about the bedroom that awaited me. So, I set out on a mission to emulate the oasis-like feeling of a top-notch hotel at home. I even enlisted the help of hospitality and wellness experts to guide me on which bedroom essentials make all the difference.

Below, I’ve gathered the premium bedding, linens, and bedtime accessories used at some of the best hotels around the world. From cloud-like mattresses to plush robes and slippers, these little luxuries will help make your bedroom feel more like a five-star hotel.

articles.title: I Love When Celebrities Stan Other Celebrities
articles.summary: Stars, they’re just like us: They fangirl over other stars! (Or, sometimes, over themselves.)
body: Part of the appeal of being a celebrity, I’d argue, is the global adoration and sea of nameless fans that come along with fame. There is an unimaginable thrill to knowing there are thousands—if not millions—of people out there obsessed with your work. But one has to wonder... are stars ever stars to other stars? (Meta!) Do A-listers lose their minds at the sight of fellow A-listers? How does that work?

A quick trip down memory lane would prove that the answer is an unresounding yes. And to prove their own celeb-on-celeb adoration, many a famous person has stepped out in a cheeky tee that proudly displays said love for one another.
Alexander Skarsgard wearing Chopova Lowena—a chic homage to Olivia Colman on his shirt.

Just this week, for instance, Alexander Skarsgard hit the Los Angeles premiere of Wicker bearing a chic homage to his co-star, Olivia Colman. The full Chopova Lowena look (with a graphic skirt!) was fun, edgy, and all about that custom tee with Colman’s face on it.
